title: Indian Techie Dies in California After Valley Fever Battle
excerpt: Chiranjeevi Kolla, 37, passed away on May 5 after a month in ICU — leaving behind a wife and a five-year-old son.
body:
Chiranjeevi Kolla, a 37-year-old Indian software professional based in Walnut Creek, California, died on May 5 after spending nearly a month on a ventilator fighting Valley fever — a fungal lung infection caused by inhaling microscopic soil spores. He leaves behind his wife, Pavani Marella, and their five-year-old son, Vihan.

**What happened:**
Kolla first fell ill in early April with what appeared to be ordinary flu-like symptoms. When his condition kept worsening, he visited the emergency room, where doctors initially suspected severe pneumonia. Further tests confirmed Valley fever — a fungal infection caused by *Coccidioides* spores found in California's soil — by which point the infection had overwhelmed his lungs. He died at Kaiser Permanente in Walnut Creek after thirty days in intensive care.

**Why this matters now:**
California recorded nearly 12,500 Valley fever cases in 2024 — the highest figure on record in state history — and the California Department of Public Health has warned that case counts remain elevated in 2025. The CDC estimates the true national burden may reach 206,000 to 360,000 cases per year, many never properly diagnosed because early symptoms mimic the flu. Delayed diagnosis, as in Kolla's case, dramatically raises the risk of fatal respiratory failure. Populations arriving from South Asia have no prior immunity or awareness of this soil-borne hazard, making the threat especially acute for the Indian tech workforce concentrated in California's Bay Area and Central Valley.

**What to watch:**
Public health advocates are now calling for mandatory Valley fever awareness briefings for newly arrived immigrant workers in endemic regions — watch whether California's CDPH or employers in the tech sector take any formal steps in response.
